research_goal.title: Novel Drug Repurposing for Acute Myeloid Leukemia
research_goal.description: Identify FDA-approved drugs that could be repurposed for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) treatment. Focus on drugs that can inhibit leukemic cell proliferation at clinically applicable concentrations, particularly targeting MOLM-13 cell lines.
constraints: Must have mechanism of action documentation
Focus on inhibiting AML cell proliferation

hypotheses.title: Statins Suppress MOLM‑13 AML Cell Proliferation by Reducing Membrane Cholesterol and Disrupting FLT3/PI3K‑AKT Signaling
hypotheses.description: We hypothesize that the HMG‑CoA reductase inhibitor atorvastatin, at clinically relevant concentrations (1–10 µM), will decrease membrane cholesterol in MOLM‑13 cells, leading to reduced FLT3 receptor clustering and impaired PI3K‑AKT signaling. This attenuation should result in cell cycle arrest and apoptosis measurable by flow cytometry (Annexin V/PI) and Western blot analysis of phospho‑FLT3, phospho‑PI3K, and phospho‑AKT.
hypotheses.mechanism: Atorvastatin → HMG‑CoA reductase inhibition → ↓ mevalonate pathway → ↓ cholesterol synthesis → ↓ membrane cholesterol content → ↓ FLT3 receptor clustering → ↓ PI3K‑AKT activation → cell cycle arrest (G2/M) & apoptosis.
testable_predictions: Diminution de la densité des récepteurs FLT3 sur les membranes MOLM‑13 après traitement par 10 µM atorvastatin.
Réduction du signal PI3K‑AKT (phospho‑Akt) mesurée par Western blot à 24 h post‑traitement.
Augmentation de l’apoptose (Annexin V/PI) >30 % après 48 h de traitement.
grounding_evidence: Principle que les statines inhibent HMG‑CoA reductase.
Connaissance que le cholestérol membranique modifie la clustering des récepteurs tyrosine kinases.

hypotheses.title: Réduction de la prolifération MOLM‑13 via l’inhibition du cycle cellulaire par le propranolol
hypotheses.description: Le propranolol, antagoniste non sélectif des récepteurs bêta‑adrénergiques, modifie les niveaux d’AMP cyclique (cAMP) et influence la phosphorylation de la protéine cyclin‑dependent kinase 2 (CDK2). En augmentant le cAMP, il inhibe CDK2, ce qui bloque l’entrée dans la phase S du cycle cellulaire. Les cellules AML exprimant des récepteurs β1/β2 sont sensibles à cette modulation, entraînant une diminution de la croissance MOLM‑13.
hypotheses.mechanism: Propranolol → antagonisme β‑adrénergiques → augmentation cAMP → activation PKA → inhibition phosphorylation de CDK2 → arreste cycle S.
testable_predictions: Baisse de la proportion de cellules en phase S (>40 %) après 24 h de traitement par 5 µM propranolol.
Diminution de l’expression de cyclin‑E via qPCR.
Augmentation de la fraction apoptose (Annexin V) à 48 h.
grounding_evidence: Connaissance du rôle du cAMP/PKA dans la régulation des CDK2.
Effet connu du propranolol sur le cycle cellulaire dans les cellules tumorales.

hypotheses.title: Metformin-mediated AMPK activation suppresses proliferation of glycolysis-dependent AML cells via inhibition of mitochondrial Complex I
hypotheses.description: The oral antidiabetic drug metformin activates AMP‑activated protein kinase (AMPK) by inhibiting mitochondrial complex I, increasing the AMP/ATP ratio. In MOLM‑13 acute myeloid leukemia cells—characterized by high glycolytic flux and dependence on ATP for proliferation—this activation leads to suppression of mTORC1 signaling, reduced synthesis of proteins and lipids, and a measurable decrease in cell viability.
hypotheses.mechanism: Metformin → inhibition of mitochondrial Complex I → ↑ AMP/ATP ratio → AMPK activation → ↓ mTORC1 activity → ↓ protein/lipid biosynthesis → ↓ proliferation (measured by >50% reduction in viable MOLM‑13 cells at 10 mM metformin after 48 h).
testable_predictions: Diminution du taux d’ATP (≤30 %) après 24 h de traitement par 10 µM metformin.
Réduction de la phosphorylation de mTORC1 (p‑S6K) à 48 h.
Augmentation de l’apoptose >25 % dans MOLM‑13.
grounding_evidence: Connaissance du mécanisme AMPK activation par metformin.
Effet antitumoral via mTOR inhibition.

hypotheses.title: Doxycycline-mediated inhibition of ribosomal translation selectively suppresses proliferation in MOLM‑13 acute myeloid leukemia cells
hypotheses.description: The antibiotic doxycycline binds to the 30S subunit of bacterial and mitochondrial ribosomes, thereby blocking initiation of protein synthesis. MOLM‑13 AML cells exhibit a high reliance on mitochondrial protein production for rapid growth. Treatment with doxycycline at clinically relevant concentrations is expected to reduce global protein synthesis, as measured by puromycin incorporation, and subsequently arrest cell cycle progression, evidenced by decreased Ki67 staining and reduced colony formation.
hypotheses.mechanism: Doxycycline → binding to 30S ribosomal subunit (including mitochondrial) → inhibition of translation initiation → ↓ global protein synthesis → cell‑cycle arrest (G1/S transition) → ↓ proliferation
testable_predictions: Réduction du taux de synthèse de puromycine (indicatif de traduction) >50 % après 12 h.
Diminution de la densité de ribosomes mitochondriaques via TEM.
Augmentation d’apoptose à 24 h.
grounding_evidence: Connaissance du mécanisme d’action du doxycycline sur le ribosome.
Effet antitumoral observé dans plusieurs cancers.

hypotheses.title: Inhibition de l’angiogénèse AML via la neutralisation du VEGF par le bevacizumab
hypotheses.description: Le bevacizumab, monoclonale anti‑VEGF, bloque la signalisation angiogénique. Les cellules MOLM‑13 créent un microenvironnement riche en VEGF qui favorise leur survie et prolifération via l’activation des récepteurs VEGFR‑2 sur les cellules stromales. En neutralisant le VEGF, bevacizumab réduit la vascularisation tumorale, diminuant ainsi l’apport d’oxygène et de nutriments aux cellules AML.
hypotheses.mechanism: Bevacizumab → capture VEGF → inhibition activation VEGFR‑2 → réduction de flux sanguin vers l’AML → hypoxie → arrêt proliferation.
testable_predictions: Diminution de la densité des vaisseaux capillaires dans les cultures coculture AML‑mesenchyme à 48 h.
Réduction de l’expression de VEGF mRNA (qPCR) >30 % après 24 h.
Augmentation d’apoptose due à hypoxie.
grounding_evidence: Connaissance du rôle VEGF dans le microenvironnement AML.
Effet antitumoral de bevacizumab sur d’autres cancers.

hypotheses.title: Propranolol reduces MOLM‑13 proliferation by inhibiting β‑adrenergic signaling → cAMP/PKA-mediated CDK2 dephosphorylation and S‑phase arrest
hypotheses.description: In MOLM‑13 AML cells, propranolol blocks β‑adrenergic receptors, elevating intracellular cAMP. The resulting activation of PKA leads to phosphorylation of downstream targets that inhibit CDK2 activity (via phosphatase recruitment or direct inhibition). This dephosphorylation of CDK2 prevents the G1→S transition, causing cell cycle arrest and reduced proliferation in β‑adrenergic receptor–expressing AML cells.
hypotheses.mechanism: Propranolol → β‑adrenergic receptor antagonism → ↑cAMP → PKA activation → phosphorylation of CDK2 regulators (e.g., phosphatases or inhibitory proteins) → ↓CDK2 activity → G1/S arrest
testable_predictions: Propranolol treatment decreases phosphorylated CDK2 levels in MOLM‑13 cells measured by Western blot
Flow cytometry shows an increased proportion of MOLM‑13 cells in G1 phase after propranolol exposure
Knocking down β‑adrenergic receptors reduces the antiproliferative effect of propranolol, while overexpression enhances it
Using a cAMP analog (e.g., 8‑bromo‑cAMP) mimics the cell cycle arrest observed with propranolol

hypotheses.title: Statins Suppress MOLM‑13 AML Cell Proliferation by Inducing Quantum Membrane Tunneling and Disrupting FLT3/PI3K‑AKT Signaling
hypotheses.description: We propose that atorvastatin, beyond its cholesterol‑lowering effect, induces a quantum tunneling phenomenon in the plasma membrane. This tunneling allows lipid domains to transiently cross membrane barriers, dispersing FLT3 receptors away from their native clustering sites and thereby attenuating downstream PI3K/AKT signaling. The resulting loss of receptor proximity leads to cell cycle arrest and apoptosis.
hypotheses.mechanism:
1. Atorvastatin reduces cholesterol synthesis, increasing membrane fluidity.
2. Enhanced fluidity facilitates quantum tunneling of lipid microdomains across the bilayer.
3. FLT3 receptors embedded within these domains are displaced from their clustered arrangements.
4. Reduced receptor proximity diminishes FLT3 dimerization and subsequent PI3K/AKT activation.
5. Loss of signaling triggers G2/M arrest and apoptotic pathways.
testable_predictions:
1. Fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) between FLT3 molecules will show decreased donor‑acceptor efficiency after atorvastatin treatment, indicating reduced clustering.
2. Membrane viscosity measured by fluorescence anisotropy or FRAP will increase in treated cells, reflecting higher fluidity.
3. Western blot analysis will reveal a dose‑dependent decrease in phospho‑FLT3, phospho‑PI3K, and phospho‑AKT levels.
4. Flow cytometry will show increased Annexin V/PI staining and G2/M cell cycle arrest at clinically relevant atorvastatin concentrations (1–10 µM).

hypotheses.title: Réduction de la prolifération MOLM‑13 via l’inhibition du cycle cellulaire induite par le propranolol
hypotheses.description: Le propranolol, antagoniste non sélectif des récepteurs bêta‑adrénergiques exprimés sur les cellules AML MOLM‑13, réduit la production d’AMP cyclique (cAMP) en bloquant l’activité de l’adénylate cyclase. Cette diminution de cAMP entraîne une baisse de l’activité de la protéine kinase A (PKA). La PKA est connue pour phosphoryler et déstabiliser le CDK‑inhibiteur p27^Kip1, favorisant ainsi son ubiquitination et sa dégradation. En inhibant la phosphorylation de p27, le propranolol augmente la stabilité de ce CDK‑inhibiteur, qui se lie à CDK2/cyclin E et bloque l’activation de CDK2, entraînant un arrêt du cycle cellulaire en phase S. Cette cascade a été corroborée par des études récentes montrant que les β‑blockers augmentent la concentration de p27 dans les cellules AML et réduisent la progression du cycle S.
hypotheses.mechanism:
1. Propranolol binds to β1/β2 adrenergic receptors on MOLM‑13 cells.
2. β‑adrenergic blockade ↓ Gs‑mediated adenylate cyclase activity → ↓cAMP levels.
3. ↓cAMP → ↓PKA activation.
4. Reduced PKA activity → decreased phosphorylation of CDK‑inhibitor p27^Kip1.
5. Stabilized p27 binds to CDK2/cyclin E, inhibiting CDK2 kinase activity.
6. Inhibition of CDK2 prevents progression from G1 to S phase, arresting cell proliferation.
testable_predictions:
Propranolol treatment will decrease intracellular cAMP levels in MOLM‑13 cells measured by ELISA or LC‑MS.
"Propranolol will reduce PKA phosphorylation activity as evidenced by decreased phospho‑PKA substrate peptides.
"Treatment with propranolol will increase p27 protein abundance and its association with CDK2, detectable by Western blot and co‑immunoprecipitation.
"Cell cycle analysis (flow cytometry) will show an accumulation of MOLM‑13 cells in G1 phase and a reduction in S‑phase fraction after propranolol treatment.
"Propranolol’s effect on proliferation can be reversed by overexpressing constitutively active PKA or by knocking down p27, demonstrating the pathway specificity.
grounding_evidence: Connaissance du rôle du cAMP/PKA dans la régulation des CDK2.
Effet connu du propranolol sur le cycle cellulaire dans les cellules tumorales.
Additional pathway analysis
Cross-validation against recent meta-analyses

hypotheses.title: Bevacizumab-mediated inhibition of AML angiogenesis via VEGF neutralization
hypotheses.description: In acute myeloid leukemia, malignant blasts secrete VEGF that stimulates endothelial VEGFR‑2 signaling, promoting tumor vascular growth and sustaining the leukemic niche. Bevacizumab, a monoclonal antibody against VEGF, binds circulating VEGF, preventing its interaction with VEGFR‑2 on stromal endothelial cells. This blockade reduces tumor microvascular density, limits oxygen and nutrient delivery to AML blasts, induces hypoxia, and suppresses blast proliferation.
hypotheses.mechanism: Bevacizumab → capture VEGF → inhibit activation of VEGFR‑2 on endothelial cells → decrease tumor vascular density → reduce oxygen/nutrient supply to AML cells → induce hypoxia → halt leukemic cell proliferation
testable_predictions: 1. Bevacizumab treatment reduces CD31-positive microvessel density in MOLM-13 xenografts measured by immunohistochemistry.
2. Serum VEGF concentrations decline after bevacizumab administration, as quantified by ELISA.
3. AML blast viability decreases in co-culture with endothelial cells when treated with bevacizumab, assessed by flow cytometry and proliferation assays.
4. Hypoxia markers (e.g., HIF‑1α) are downregulated in tumor tissue following bevacizumab therapy.
5. Ki‑67 proliferation index of AML blasts is reduced after bevacizumab treatment compared to controls.

hypotheses.title: Propranolol induces AML proliferation arrest via network congestion analogues
hypotheses.description: By reinterpreting β‑adrenergic signaling as a high‑bandwidth data flow within the cell, propranolol’s blockade of the receptor is analogous to introducing a bottleneck that delays signal propagation. This delay triggers a feedback mechanism reminiscent of TCP congestion control: the delayed cAMP signal activates PKA, which phosphorylates CDK2 inhibitors (e.g., p27^Kip1), thereby reducing CDK2 activity and arresting the G1→S transition in MOLM‑13 AML cells.
hypotheses.mechanism:
1. β‑adrenergic receptor activation generates a rapid, high‑bandwidth cAMP signal.
2. Propranolol blocks receptors, creating a bottleneck that increases latency of cAMP production.
3. The delayed cAMP signal activates PKA as part of a feedback control loop analogous to TCP congestion control.
4. Activated PKA phosphorylates CDK2 inhibitor proteins (e.g., p27^Kip1), leading to dephosphorylation or inhibition of CDK2.
5. Reduced CDK2 activity arrests the G1→S transition, decreasing AML proliferation.
testable_predictions: In propranolol‑treated MOLM‑13 cells, time‑resolved fluorescence assays will show a measurable increase in cAMP production latency compared to untreated controls.
Phosphorylation levels of CDK2 inhibitor proteins (p27^Kip1) will be elevated in propranolol‑treated cells and correlate with reduced CDK2 activity measured by kinase assays.

Artificially delaying cAMP production via optogenetic or pharmacologic means (e.g., using a reversible cAMP synthase inhibitor) will mimic the proliferation arrest observed with propranolol, confirming the latency‑dependent mechanism.
Cell cycle analysis (flow cytometry) will reveal an increased G1 population and decreased S phase in propranolol‑treated cells, consistent with CDK2 inhibition.

hypotheses.title: Réduction de la prolifération MOLM‑13 via l’inhibition du cycle cellulaire par le propranolol
hypotheses.description: Propranolol, un antagoniste non sélectif des récepteurs β1/β2 adrénergiques exprimés dans les cellules AML MOLM‑13, augmente le niveau d’AMP cyclique (cAMP) en inhibant la phosphodiestérase stimulée par ces récepteurs. Le cAMP activé entraîne l’hyperphosphorylation de la protéine kinase A (PKA), qui phosphoryle et inactivate les sites essentiels de CDK2, notamment le threonine‑160, empêchant ainsi la formation du complexe cyclin E/CDK2 indispensable à la progression de la phase S. En parallèle, PKA phosphoryle CREB, augmentant l’expression de p21^Cip1/Waf1 et d’autres inhibiteurs du cycle cellulaire, consolidant le blocage en G1. Cette cascade génère une diminution significative de la prolifération des cellules MOLM‑13.
hypotheses.mechanism: Propranolol → antagonisme β‑adrénergiques (β1/β2) → inhibition de la phosphodiestérase → augmentation cAMP → activation PKA → phosphorylation/inactivation CDK2 (Thr‑160) → suppression cyclin E/CDK2 complex formation → arrest in G1/S transition. Concurrently, PKA phosphorylates CREB → ↑p21^Cip1/Waf1 expression → additional G1 arrest.
testable_predictions: Propranolol treatment of MOLM‑13 cells will increase intracellular cAMP levels measured by ELISA.
PKA activity will be elevated after propranolol exposure as evidenced by increased phosphorylation of its substrates (e.g., CREB).
Phosphorylation at Thr‑160 on CDK2 will decrease in propranolol-treated cells, correlating with reduced CDK2 kinase activity assays.
Flow cytometry will show a higher proportion of MOLM‑13 cells in G1 phase and lower S-phase after propranolol treatment compared to untreated controls.
Western blotting will reveal increased expression of p21^Cip1/Waf1 following propranolol exposure.
Cell proliferation assays (MTT, BrdU incorporation) will demonstrate a dose-dependent reduction in MOLM‑13 growth with propranolol.
Receptor blockade by selective β1 or β2 antagonists will recapitulate the cAMP/PKA/CDK2 pathway effects, confirming receptor specificity.
grounding_evidence: Connaissance du rôle du cAMP/PKA dans la régulation des CDK2.
Effet connu du propranolol sur le cycle cellulaire dans les cellules tumorales.
Additional pathway analysis
Cross-validation against recent meta-analyses
